algae_description: Fine, wispy green algae strands visible on the mesh bag surface and scattered lightly around the midground. Floating plants (likely frogbit or duckweed) are dense at the water surface. Growth appears modest and characteristic of a maturing cycle tank.
substrate_condition: Clay-based lava rock / LECA substrate visible — dark spherical pellets covering the bottom. A large mesh bag (likely containing substrate or mineral media) dominates the foreground. Substrate beneath and around the bag appears undisturbed and clean.
concerns: Mesh bag occupying significant tank floor space — worth monitoring to ensure shrimp can navigate around and beneath it freely
Floating plant surface coverage appears dense — may begin to limit light penetration to lower plants if it continues spreading unchecked
narrative: Day 49 of the nitrogen cycle and the tank is clearly coming into its own — lush floating plants crowd the surface, a healthy cluster of green aquatic plants anchors the left midground, and a large mesh bag (mineralizing substrate or media?) takes up much of the foreground floor. One shrimp — red-orange, adult-sized — is just barely visible at the lower right corner near the bag, a quiet cameo in an otherwise equipment-forward frame. Water reads clear, and the overall scene has the comfortable density of a tank that's been growing steadily.
image_subject: Full tank interior shot, low angle, foreground dominated by a large mesh media/substrate bag; equipment visible includes a blue thermometer or CO2 indicator (left), a circulation pump or powerhead (center-rear), and a hang-on-back or sponge filter with ceramic media visible (right)

algae_description: Fine green algae or biofilm visible clinging to the underside of the water surface and trailing downward — a healthy sign of an actively cycling tank. Some loose plant or algae strands also appear scattered near the mesh bag on the substrate.
substrate_condition: Dark, rounded substrate granules (appears to be lava rock or black aqua soil) covering the tank floor. A large mesh media bag sits directly on the substrate — likely containing lava rock or ceramic bio-media. Substrate looks undisturbed and clean.
image_subject: Interior tank shot, low-angle view showing substrate, hardscape equipment, and a media bag in the foreground; a moss clump (likely java moss or similar), a heater, a sponge filter with ceramic/clay media balls visible, and the water surface with algae growth above.
concerns: Large mesh media bag sitting directly on the substrate — unclear if this is intentional (cycling media, mineral buffer, etc.) or something that should be removed before shrimp fully colonize the tank floor
Loose plant/algae fragments scattered on substrate near the bag — minor, but worth monitoring for debris buildup
narrative: Day 49 of the nitrogen cycle and the tank is showing encouraging signs of biological life — fine green algae has colonized the water surface and equipment, which is exactly what a maturing cycle looks like. The dominant foreground feature is a large mesh bag resting on the dark substrate, likely holding cycling media or mineral material; a healthy-looking moss clump sits behind it, and the filter assembly with clay/ceramic bio-balls is clearly visible to the right.
